st: Bring [[3 cup]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Mix [[1 cup]] of the cornmeal with the remaining [[1 cup]] cold water in a bowl to a smooth slurry.
Stir the slurry into the boiling water and cook 5 minutes until it thickens like pudding.
Reduce to low heat and cover for 10 minutes.
Add the remaining [[1 cup]] cornmeal a little at a time, stirring hard with a wooden spoon so it does not lump.
Cover and cook on low 10 more minutes, stirring now and then, until very stiff.
Wet a bowl, scoop the porridge into it, and turn out a firm mound. Serve with stew, meat or greens.
Warm [[4 cup]] milk in a pan to about 110°F (43°C), lukewarm and not hot.
Pour it into a clean glass jar and stir in [[2 tbsp]] yogurt.
Cover loosely and keep in a warm spot for 12 hours, until thick and tangy.
Refrigerate the emasi until cold, at least 2 hours.
Boil [[2 cup]] water with [[0.25 tsp]] salt. Stir in [[1 cup]] cornmeal slowly and cook on low for 10 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Spoon the warm porridge into bowls and pour cold emasi over it.
Put the pumpkin in a pot with [[2 cup]] water and [[0.25 tsp]] salt. Boil for 20 minutes until very soft.
Mash the pumpkin in its liquid with a fork or masher until mostly smooth.
Add [[1 cup]] milk and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Slowly sprinkle in [[0.75 cup]] cornmeal while stirring so no lumps form.
Cook on low for 15 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] butter and [[1 tbsp]] sugar if you like it sweet. Serve warm.

ing: cut in long strips along the grain
st: Slice the beef into strips about 1 inch thick and 8 inches long, cutting along the grain. Trim off most of the fat.
Lay the strips in a glass dish and pour over [[0.25 cup]] vinegar. Turn to coat and let sit for 30 minutes.
Mix [[2 tbsp]] salt, [[2 tbsp]] coriander, [[1 tbsp]] pepper and [[1 tbsp]] sugar. Rub it thoroughly onto every strip.
Cover and refrigerate for 12 hours so the cure sinks in.
Hang the strips with hooks or skewers in a dry, airy place, or in an oven at its lowest setting (about 170°F/75°C) with the door cracked open.
Dry for 8 hours in the oven, or 4 days hanging in a cool dry spot, until firm and a bit bendy, and cut slices look dark inside.
Store the finished umncweba in a paper bag in the refrigerator. Slice thin to eat, and use within 1 week.
Soak the beans in water overnight, at least 8 hours, then drain.
Put the beans in a pot with [[5 cup]] fresh water. Bring to a boil and simmer for 60 minutes until soft.
Meanwhile, toast the peanuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 6 minutes, stirring, until lightly browned. Cool them.
Rub off the skins and grind the peanuts coarsely in a food processor, or pound them in a mortar.
Drain the beans, keeping a little of the cooking water.
Return the beans to the pot and mash them with a potato masher. Stir in the ground peanuts and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Cook on low for 10 minutes, adding cooking water a spoonful at a time, until a thick mash forms. Serve warm.
Toast the peanuts in a dry skillet for 6 minutes until golden, cool, then grind them to a coarse powder.
Wash the greens well and chop them. Strip tough stems from pumpkin leaves if using.
Boil the greens in water for 10 minutes until tender, then drain and squeeze out the water.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook 6 minutes until soft.
Add the greens, [[1 cup]] water and [[0.75 tsp]] salt. Stir and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the ground peanuts and cook 5 minutes more, until the sauce is thick. Serve with sishwala.
